asks: When a program sends many held requests at once, how many asks do you get?
answer: One open ask per computer. A request a rule holds joins the computer's open ask if you have not answered it yet, and otherwise opens a new one, which waits 2 seconds to gather the rest of its burst before it reaches you. Each version of the list has a number, and your answer covers exactly the requests of the version you saw, each once. A request held after your answer opens the next ask. A request that a program sends again after its own timeout joins the line it repeats, when the boundary can tell it is the same one: the same request id from the AWS SDK, or the same method, host, path and body within 120 seconds. A yes lets pass only its newest copy. A burst still makes as many asks as the program has steps that wait on each other.
